title: Luchi Alur Dom
steps: Knead maida with salt, ghee and water into a soft dough. Rest 20 mins.
Boil baby potatoes, peel and keep whole or halve.
Heat mustard oil, temper panch phoron and green chillies. Add ginger paste, tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, cumin and salt. Cook till oil separates.
Add potatoes, sugar and a little water. Cover and simmer till gravy thickens and coats the potatoes.
Roll small portions of dough into thin circles and deep-fry in hot oil till puffed and golden (luchi).
Serve hot luchis with alur dom.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Use Chandramukhi or new potatoes for authentic taste.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Do not over-knead the dough; soft dough gives softer luchis.

title: Kochuri with Cholar Dal
steps: Soak urad dal, grind with ginger, green chilli and fennel into a coarse paste. Season and keep ready for stuffing.
Knead maida dough, rest. Stuff small portions with dal paste, roll and deep-fry into kochuri.
Pressure-cook chana dal till soft. Temper whole spices in ghee, add coconut, raisins, cooked dal, sugar and salt. Simmer till thick and aromatic.
Serve hot kochuri with cholar dal.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil or ghee for frying

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Radhaballavi is a close variant with different stuffing; both are festive breakfast classics.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A little sugar in the dal balances the spices.

title: Panta Bhat
steps: Place leftover cooked rice in a bowl and cover completely with clean water.
Leave overnight at room temperature to ferment slightly.
Next morning, drain excess water if desired (or keep some), mash lightly, add salt, chopped green chillies and a drizzle of mustard oil.
Serve plain or with fried vegetables, pickles or (non-Jain) onion.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional summer breakfast; cooling and probiotic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: For strict Jain version omit onion.

title: Shukto
steps: Cut all vegetables into batons. Lightly fry bitter gourd and bori separately.
Heat mustard oil + ghee, temper panch phoron/radhuni. Add ginger paste and vegetables. Sauté briefly.
Add salt, sugar, mustard paste, a little water. Cover and cook till vegetables are tender.
Stir in milk and poppy paste if using. Simmer 2-3 minutes. Finish with fried bori.
Serve as the first course with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bitterness is intentional and aids digestion; balance with milk and a pinch of sugar.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Seasonal vegetables change the character of the dish.

title: Aloo Posto
steps: Soak poppy seeds 15-20 mins, grind with green chillies into a smooth paste adding little water.
Peel and cube potatoes. Heat mustard oil till smoking, cool slightly, add kalonji.
Add potatoes, turmeric and salt. Sauté on medium heat till almost cooked.
Add posto paste and a splash of water. Cook covered till oil separates and potatoes are coated in creamy paste.
Adjust sugar if desired. Serve with steamed rice and dal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Authentic versions are quite dry and creamy rather than watery.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is essential for the classic flavour.

title: Shorshe Ilish
steps: Marinate hilsa with salt and half the turmeric for 15 mins.
Grind mustard seeds with green chillies and a little water into a smooth paste (do not over-grind or it becomes bitter).
Heat mustard oil, temper nigella and a couple of green chillies. Add remaining turmeric and the mustard paste. Stir on low heat.
Add a little water to make gravy, then gently slide in the fish pieces. Cover and cook on low for 8-10 mins without stirring much.
Finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil. Serve with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Hilsa is seasonal (monsoon); use fresh fish for best results.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Never cook mustard paste on high heat for long – it turns bitter.

title: Chingri Malaikari
steps: Clean prawns, devein, keep heads if preferred. Marinate with turmeric and salt.
Lightly fry prawns and set aside.
In the same pan heat ghee/oil, add whole spices, then onion paste. Cook till golden.
Add ginger-garlic, turmeric, chilli powder and yogurt. Cook till oil separates.
Pour thin coconut milk, simmer, then add thick coconut milk and fried prawns. Cook gently 5-7 mins. Finish with garam masala and a pinch of sugar.
Serve with steamed rice or luchi.

fullIngredients.name: Garam masala, bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Golda chingri (freshwater) gives the classic rich flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Do not boil the coconut milk vigorously after adding prawns.

title: Kosha Mangsho
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric and salt for at least 2 hours (overnight preferred).
Heat mustard oil, add a pinch of sugar and caramelise. Add whole spices and sliced onions. Fry on medium-low till deep brown (this is the kosha stage).
Add marinated mutton and continue slow-frying (kosha) for 20-25 mins, stirring often, till meat changes colour and oil separates.
Add a little hot water, cover and pressure-cook or slow-cook till mutton is tender and gravy is thick and dark.
Serve with luchi, porota or steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Whole garam masala (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The dark colour comes from slow-frying onions and the sugar caramelisation.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Patience is key – true kosha cannot be rushed.

title: Dhokar Dalna
steps: Soak chana dal, grind with ginger and green chilli into a thick paste. Season, steam or shallow-fry into diamond-shaped cakes (dhoka).
Cube and fry potatoes. Make a gravy with tempered spices, onion (if using), tomato, spice powders and water.
Add fried potatoes and dhoka pieces. Simmer gently so the cakes absorb the gravy but do not break.
Finish with ghee and garam masala. Serve with rice or luchi.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Dhoka can be made ahead and stored.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A classic niramish (no onion-garlic) version exists for festive meals.

title: Jhalmuri
steps: In a large bowl or paper cone, mix muri with mustard oil so it coats lightly.
Add chopped onion, green chilli, cucumber, tomato, peanuts, bhujia, spices, lemon juice and coriander.
Toss vigorously so everything is evenly distributed. Serve immediately.

fullIngredients.name: Black salt, roasted cumin powder, chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Street-style jhalmuri is mixed and eaten on the spot so the muri stays crisp.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Omit onion for a milder version.

title: Beguni
steps: Slice brinjal into thin rounds or long slices. Lightly salt and keep aside.
Make a thick batter with besan, rice flour, spices, salt and water. Add a pinch of soda.
Dip each slice in batter and deep-fry in hot mustard oil till golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with puffed rice or as a tea-time snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil gives the authentic telebhaja flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Serve immediately for maximum crispness.

title: Puchka (Phuchka)
steps: Mash boiled potatoes with salt, black salt, cumin and chilli powder. Mix in boiled peas.
Prepare tangy-spicy tamarind water seasoned with black salt, cumin, chilli and mint if desired.
Crack a small hole on top of each puchka shell, fill with potato mixture, top with onion and coriander, then dip or pour the tamarind water.
Eat immediately in one bite.

fullIngredients.name: Boiled black chickpeas or yellow peas
Black salt, roasted cumin, chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Kolkata-style puchka has a sharper, more tangy water than Mumbai pani puri.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Freshly made shells are ideal.

title: Aloo Chop
steps: Mash boiled potatoes. Sauté onion, ginger, green chilli and spices. Mix into the mash. Shape into flat oval chops.
Dip in thin besan batter or beaten egg, roll in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in hot oil till golden brown and crisp.
Serve hot with kasundi or tomato sauce.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A classic evening snack with muri or tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fish or mutton chop versions are also popular non-veg variants.

title: Doi Chire
steps: Rinse chire briefly and drain well (or soak very lightly if thick variety).
Whisk yogurt with sugar/jaggery and a little milk if needed for pouring consistency.
Mix the drained chire into the sweetened yogurt. Add sliced banana or fruit.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A light, cooling traditional breakfast especially in summer.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Use good quality thick Bengali doi for best results.

title: Machher Jhol
steps: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry and set aside.
In the same oil fry potato wedges. Temper cumin/panch phoron, add ginger, tomato and spice powders.
Add water to make a light gravy, season, then add fried potatoes and fish.
Simmer 8-10 mins. Finish with green chillies and coriander. Serve with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The classic everyday Bengali fish curry – light, slightly spicy and runny.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is non-negotiable for authentic taste.

title: Dimer Dalna
steps: Hard-boil eggs, peel and lightly fry with turmeric till golden. Fry potato cubes separately.
Make a gravy: temper whole spices, fry onion till golden, add ginger-garlic, tomato and spice powders. Cook till oil separates.
Add water, fried potatoes and eggs. Simmer till gravy thickens slightly.
Finish with garam masala. Serve with rice or luchi.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A comforting everyday egg curry popular across Bengali homes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Some versions are made niramish (no onion-garlic) for festive days.
